sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Dresden's car parks were back to their 2023 level by 2024 and have been flat since: the last twelve months averaged 41% of spaces occupied, exactly the same as the year before, and 2026 so far is 2% below 2025, in line with Germany.

The main policy change has been the price of the street. After a first proposal that the ADAC called a doubling or more [0], the city raised on-street fees in three steps from 2021 to 2023, to €2.70 an hour in the central zone with a €12 day ticket [1], the first rise in about 15 years. A resident-parking scheme around Schillerplatz in Blasewitz, required by the 2019 air-quality plan, was still at the consultation stage when the city last updated its page in 2021 [6]. The collapse of part of the Carolabrücke in September 2024 removed a crossing used by over 30,000 vehicles a day and pushed traffic onto the other bridges [8][9]. Our numbers show only a short dip: October 2024 was 5% below October 2023, and by January occupancy was above the previous year again.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Much of the central garage capacity sits under shopping centres: the Centrum Galerie (Goldbeck, about 1,060 spaces) and the Altmarkt-Galerie (APCOA, 520) are the largest central garages. The city itself runs most of the open car parks around the old town and a ring of free park-and-ride sites, and the outer sites, mostly park-and-ride, are the part of the market that has grown: in the same garages, weekday occupancy rose from 27% in 2022 to 38% in 2025. The centre held steady (59% to 62%), while garages one to three kilometres out lost ground (32% to 24%).

On the street, the city began offering payment by smartphone at about 450 of its machines in 2019 [2], and the Altmarkt square above the Q-Park garage was rebuilt from April 2022 to October 2023 for about €11 million, with the garage staying open [7]. Elsewhere, technology is arriving through the private operators, for example ticketless entry by app at APCOA's Dresden-Mitte garage [3]. Public charging grew from 163 stations in 2019 towards a target of 400 by the end of 2022 [4][5]; we found no figures for charging in garages.

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
The market splits cleanly in two. The city's own car parks near the centre are cheap, €1.50 an hour and €6 a day at Ferdinandplatz, Reitbahnstraße and Budapester Straße, and they are full: 63–85% on weekdays, reaching 100% at the peak. Contipark's Semperoper garage, at the same price, runs at 67%. A few hundred metres away the private garages beside the Frauenkirche and the Zwinger charge €2.50–2.90 an hour and €28–30 a day, five times the city's day rate, and stand at 18–37%.

The city's car parks are priced well below both the private garages and the central street rate [1], and they are the ones that fill. The private garages appear to work as the overflow, used by visitors who pay for being closest to the sights. APCOA's large Dresden-Mitte garage 1.3 km out (€1.50 an hour) is almost empty on weekdays (12%).
